title: Seven killed, three of them children, as truck runs over villagers helping rider in Khunti
dek: The 18-wheeler hit people gathered on the Karra-Torpa road in Jharkhand on Thursday night. Residents blocked the road on Friday demanding the driver's arrest and compensation.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Seven people, including three children according to most reports, were killed when a speeding trailer truck ran over villagers who had gathered to help a fallen scooter rider in Jharkhand's Khunti district on Thursday night, police said. One child was injured.

The accident happened at about 10 pm on the Karra-Torpa main road near the Jone-Ludru turn, under Karra police station. Six people died at the spot and one, a 12-year-old boy, died during treatment at Khunti Sadar Hospital, according to Superintendent of Police Rishabh Garg and several reports.

## What happened

A scooter rider had lost control and fallen into a roadside ditch. Villagers came out to help: young men tried to pull him out while women and children stood at the roadside, reports said.

"In the meantime, an 18-wheel truck from Torpa ran over them while taking a sharp turn," the SP told reporters. "Seven people died, and one was injured." He said the driver might not have seen the crowd in the dark. The truck then broke through a culvert and fell into a ditch, reports said.

Most reports said the dead were four women and three children; one police breakdown gave three women, three children and a man. Reports also differ on whether one or two people were injured. The dead came from two families, according to one report. The condition of the scooter rider has not been reported.

The driver and his helper fled. Police have seized the truck and are searching for them, reports said. No arrest had been reported by Friday afternoon. Some residents alleged the driver was drunk; this has not been confirmed.

## Protest and reactions

On Friday morning residents burned tyres and blocked the road near the Karra railway crossing, demanding the driver's arrest, government jobs for the victims' families, compensation and safety measures at the turn, which they said had poor visibility and heavy, fast traffic. Police and officials held talks with them and promised help and compensation "as per government provisions", reports said. No amount had been announced by Friday afternoon.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in a post from his office: "Deeply pained by the loss of lives in a mishap in Khunti, Jharkhand. I extend my condolences to those who have lost their loved ones. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured." President Droupadi Murmu also expressed condolences to the bereaved families.

Chief Minister Hemant Soren wrote that "the heartbreaking news of seven people losing their lives in a road accident in Karra, Khunti, has deeply saddened me", and prayed that Marang Buru, a deity revered by several tribal communities in Jharkhand, grant peace to the dead.

## What happens next

Police are searching for the driver and his helper. Officials have not said when compensation will be announced or whether safety work will be done at the Jone-Ludru turn, as residents demand.
